1 big thing: DOJ sues to delay Alaska results
 
Photo illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios. Photo: Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images

The Trump administration sued Alaska today to delay certification of next month's Senate election results if incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, Axios' Avery Lotz reports.

  • The race between incumbent Sullivan, Democrat Mary Peltola and retired teacher Dan Sullivan — which could determine Senate control — has been marked by controversy.

🤔 Republicans accuse Democrats of trying to confuse voters by planting a candidate with the same name as the incumbent.

  • The retired teacher Sullivan will appear on the ballot as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.
  • Alaska's use of ranked-choice voting complicates matters, eliminating candidates in rounds if no one gets 50% of the initial vote.

The lawsuit, filed in Alaska District Court, says: "An election result may be impacted by voter confusion if: (1) Senator Sullivan does not win the election; and (2) had all votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan been cast instead for Senator Sullivan and Alaska's ranked-choice process played out accordingly, Senator Sullivan would have won the election."

  • It requests a delay in certification until after an investigation determines "whether votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan."
  • President Trump personally ordered the lawsuit to be filed, AP reports.

🗳️ The big picture: The Trump administration is pushing for greater control of state-run elections and casting doubt ahead of time on results that may favor Democrats.

✅ Reality check: Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller tells AP that the Alaska suit won't survive long, since the statute "simply doesn't let the Department of Justice enjoin certification."

2. 🛸 Strange "black triangle" in new UFO docs
 
Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios

On a recent evening near a secure U.S. facility, three federal agents say they saw a flying "matte black triangle" that moved as fast as a fighter jet, made no sound and then disappeared, Axios' Marc Caputo writes from new FBI and Defense Department reports.

  • The two reports are included in a batch of documents released today by U.S. officials under President Trump's order to disclose Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena records.

🔺 The agents reported seeing the drone-like triangle, with a wingspan of about 15 feet, rise vertically for as many as 300 feet above a mountain ridgeline without tilting or swaying.

  • They say it stopped, hovered for about 20 seconds, then flew horizontally for about 1.5 miles in three seconds without making a sound. Then it simply vanished.

✅ Reality check: The records don't say whether the government believes UAPs are tied to alien life.

4. ⚾️ 1 sports thing: Fall Classic begins
 
The Brewers celebrate a game-winning hit against the San Diego Padres on Oct. 4. Photo: John Fisher/Getty Images

The World Series gets underway tonight, with the Tampa Bay Rays taking on the Milwaukee Brewers at 8 p.m. ET.

  • The series pits two smaller markets against each other, with both teams reaching baseball's biggest stage despite ranking in the bottom half of MLB payrolls, Axios Tampa Bay's Yacob Reyes writes.

🏆 Milwaukee finished with the league's best record at 103-59. They swept the two-time defending champion Dodgers to reach their first World Series since 1982.

  • Tampa Bay led the American League with 98 wins before beating Cleveland in six games to clinch their third pennant in franchise history.
